newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Aug 1.

text.p: Peters rejects super review findings: Treasurer Winston Peters put a brave face on Thursday on a review calling for the retention of New Zealand Superannuation, saying it proved the present system was unsustainable. Page 1.

Todd report praised for giving balance to pension debate: The Todd report would provide balance to the debate about the proposed compulsory retirement savings scheme, Independent Referendum Panel chairman Sir John Robertson said on Thursday. Page 2.

English will not tolerate 'political obstruction': Health Minister Bill English drew his own line in the sand on Thursday, putting both associate minister Neil Kirton and his own party on notice that he would not tolerate coalition politics obstructing health policy. Page 2.

PM's leadership under scrutiny at party conference: Prime Minister Jim Bolger's political future will face scrutiny at the National Party's annual conference starting today, even though leadership is not on the agenda. Page 2.
Analysts expect support for AMP float: AMP's mooted property float would be well-received by the market, analysts said on Thursday. Page 11.

CDL group interims show tough market: CDL Hotels, Kingsgate International and CDL Investments on Thursday reported half-year results, with the local hotel operation feeling the pressure in the local tourism market. Page 11.
Development of own sites key to Mainfreight growth: Developing properties for its own use will be the cornerstone for Mainfreight's medium-term growth. Page 14.
Shareholders approve Strathmore buy-back: Strathmore Group will proceed with a buy-back proposal. Page 14.
NZ woman feared lost amid rubble of Thredbo: Police believe a New Zealand woman was among 18 people at the Bimbadeen Lodge in Australia at the time of the landslide.

Henry stays put: Graham Henry is staying with the New Zealand rugby scene, and negotiating another two years as the Auckland Blues coach, but he predicts an exodus of top coaches to take charge of other international sides.

Bolton risks the chop as Maine disappoints: Murray Bolton's job as chief executive and chairman of Maine Investments is thought to be under threat in the wake of a major restructuring of the company's operations by its main shareholder Goldman Sachs.

Clear allowed to hold debts in test dispute: The High Court has ruled that Clear Communications can continue to withhold sums of around $500,000 owing to Telecom under its interconnection agreement, pending judgement in a full trial of the landmark case.
